run_inputs.note: Operator inputs and ordinary baseline for Slope's 14 May 2024 review of an existing line, reconstructed as if Slope opened a reusable line that pays Akoustis's supplier invoices on 1 Apr 2024. Terms reconstructed by applying Slope's published sizing rule to the connected-bank baseline. The baseline holds only ordinary underwriting facts; the litigation is for the investigation to establish.

requested_use.value: Continued draws on the existing Slope reusable line, opened on 1 Apr 2024, to pay supplier invoices (fab materials and contract manufacturing)

requested_amount.label: The next supplier invoice routed through the line after the review

requested_term.value: Reusable line; each draw repaid in three monthly installments. The line's balance and installment schedule on the review date are in the financing plan's opening state

run_inputs.initial_event_seed: As of 14 May 2024, review how external events could affect Slope's existing reusable line for Akoustis Technologies, Inc., opened on 1 Apr 2024, which pays its supplier invoices, each draw repaid in three monthly installments. Akoustis's public filings describe trade-secret and patent litigation with Qorvo, Inc., a competitor, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.

financing_plan.funding: next business day after the review date (Slope pays the supplier)
financing_plan.note: Slope pays the supplier up to the financed amount; Akoustis pays any remainder of the invoice itself.

supplied_terms.product: Slope reusable line: Slope pays supplier invoices up to the limit; each draw is repaid in monthly installments by ACH

line.label: Terms reconstructed by applying Slope's published sizing rule to the connected-bank baseline.
line.rule: limit = 15% x (mean monthly customer_receipts - mean monthly debt_service), trailing three complete months
line.reassessment: same rule at every draw date, on each trajectory's trailing receipts (next engine step)
line.draw_rule: each supplier_invoice outflow is routed while outstanding + invoice <= the day's limit, no installment is overdue and no petition has been filed

opened.basis: The earliest date with three complete months of connected-bank history in the feed (January to March 2024): Slope's rule gives 15% of mean monthly receipts net of debt service, USD 395,500.00, above the USD 250k automatic approval, so a manually reviewed line. It opens five weeks before the jury trial began on 6 May (docket as of 14 May); the trial and the 13 May 10-Q then trigger this review. Eligibility (Slope's published criteria): in business since May 2014 (FY2023 10-K: 'since its inception in May 2014'), so more than 3 years for a line above USD 100k; banking history of more than 1 year (the company's own accounts; the feed reconstructs only the months the rule reads); no bankruptcy in the last 5 years.

supplied_draw.basis: largest supplier invoice in the trailing window that fits under the limit

opening_state.note: The line's state on the review date, from app.analysis.history.replay: the engine's draw, limit and collection rules on the feed's own flows from the opening date.

draws.counterparty: Process gas and metals suppliers (fab materials)

common_model.note: Settings every path shares (spec §16.3). Central: the feed's historical continuation, no financing, a 30-day cash floor, Slope's automatic debit (collected in full when cash covers the installment), and daily cash processing (question spec §2.2: receipts first, then a levy, scheduled obligations in the order incurred, operating outflows up to the balance; the rest carried as arrears; cash never negative). Each scenario changes one setting and states its basis.

equity_injection.basis: A declared scenario, not the record: a plain equity injection of USD 5.0M booked on 14 Jun 2024, one month after the review. On 14 May the company was re-activating its at-the-market program (ATM Sales Agreement of 2 May 2022, USD 48.0M remaining, 10-Q of 13 May 2024); the agents have no obligation to sell, so the program fixes no amount or date. Usable capacity is probably limited by the baby-shelf cap (about one third of public float per 12 months, net of the January raise: roughly USD 9.7M, an inference, not stated before the cutoff); USD 5.0M sits inside it. The central case books no financing.

cost_plan.basis: Earnings call of 13 May 2024 (CFO): aggressive expense reduction and cost-saving measures, as well as pursuing the investment tax credits, 'all of which we estimate will reduce our operating cash flow burn rate by an additional 30% sequentially in the June quarter'. The March quarter's operating burn was USD 7,791,000; 30% of it is taken off every operating outflow except the litigation-spend proxy and debt service (14,092,000 in the March quarter), a 16.59% cut, from the day after the review to the horizon, so the June quarter's operating burn at the March run rate is about 30% below the March quarter's (USD 7.8M, itself 31% below December). Opex guided to USD 10-11M a quarter is an accrual figure and is not used. The call does not split the tax-credit refund from the cost cuts, so the whole 30% is read as lower outflows; revenue stays on its own path (guided flat to down 5%).

chips_itc_low.basis: A labelled sensitivity. Earnings call of 13 May 2024 (CEO): 'We currently estimate the amount of the refundable tax credit applicable to [Akoustis] to be between $2.8 and $4 million over the next nine to 12 months.' No date is given, so the central case books none inside the horizon. Here the low end is prorated evenly over 12 months and the part falling inside the horizon (USD 1,380,822) is booked month by month, as a one-off receipt outside the operating need.

protect_need.basis: A borrower-behaviour sensitivity (spec §16.3 Collection): the borrower keeps its next 30 days of operating need back from Slope, so Slope collects min(owed, max(0, available - need)). Slope's mechanism is the automatic debit on each due date (the central case); this is an assumption about the borrower, not the product.

cash_floor_60_days.basis: The cash floor at 60 days of operating need instead of 30 (the one alternative setting): the company's cash-floor decision, Jev's cash facts and settlement and stay capacity read it. Collections are unchanged (Slope's debit does not read the floor).

ordinary_obligations.note: Existing debt on every path (spec §16.3), carried as case inputs; the dispute model owns what triggers a change. Nothing here is booked by the operating simulation.

items.form: in cash and/or shares at the company's option
items.basis: USD 44.0M x 6% / 2 (10-Q Note 10; notes 8-K of June 2022: payable 15 Jun and 15 Dec). The 13 May S-3 registers 5,000,000 more note-interest shares for resale. 15 Jun 2024 is a Saturday. The next coupon, 15 Dec 2024, is after the horizon.

items.instrument: GDSI secured promissory note (USD 4.0M, no interest)
items.basis: Step-down to USD 1.3M on the second anniversary of the 1 Jan 2023 closing (10-Q Note 10; FY2023 10-K Note 7): no GDSI cash falls due inside the horizon unless accelerated.

common_model.runway_statement: 10-Q of 13 May 2024, Note 2 and MD&A overview: cash 'is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025', with substantial doubt about going concern. The MD&A's 'at least the next twelve months' sentence contradicts both and is not used.
common_model.legal_spend: The legal_fees category is a professional-fee PROXY (the March quarter's year-on-year rise in professional fees and property tax, 10-Q of 13 May 2024). It is the spend attributed to the dispute: it stops from the day the dispute ends (payment, settlement or vacatur); other spend continues.

object.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 — optional redemption, interest make-whole and qualifying fundamental change payments

spans.quote: The Company may redeem the Notes, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time on or after June 9, 2023 at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest on such principal, if any, up to the redemption date.

(i) on or after June 9, 2023, up to one-third of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes initially issued; (ii) on or after June 9, 2024, up to two-thirds of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes initially issued; and (iii) on or after June 9, 2025, up to 100% of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes initially issued;

the closing sale price per share of the Company’s common stock is greater than 150% of the then-effective conversion price for each of 20 consecutive days of the 30 consecutive trading day period immediately preceding the Company’s redemption notice

If any Notes are converted prior to June 9, 2025 (the “Interest Make-Whole Date”), the Company will make a payment to the holder of such Notes equal to the sum of the remaining scheduled payments of interest that would have been made on the Notes to be converted had such Notes remained outstanding from the conversion date through and including the Interest Make-Whole Date.

Subject to certain limitations, qualifying fundamental change payments will be made all in shares of common stock unless the Company gives written notice to the Note holders that it intends to make such payments either all or partially in cash.
If the Company redeems the Notes prior to the Interest Make-Whole Date, the holder will also receive an interest make-whole payment equal to the remaining scheduled interest payments

object.proposition: On the 13 May 2024 earnings call, Akoustis's general counsel said the trial was expected to go to the jury before the end of that week, that Akoustis will continue to vigorously defend, that the parties' experts' damages estimates are very disparate, and that if the jury adopts Qorvo's experts' theories an eight-figure verdict is possible, which could significantly affect the company's value, operations and ability to raise money.
object.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. management statements on the Qorvo v. Akoustis trial and likely award

spans.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days. We are and will continue to vigorously defend against Corvo's claims.
In particular, the theories used by each party's experts result in very disparate estimates of the damages alleged by Corvo.

However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
Cuervo's claims of false patent marking and RICO claims were dropped before trial, which is good news.
We are still early in case procedures.

object.proposition: In the proposed final jury instructions the parties disputed the trade-secret unjust enrichment measure: Akoustis proposed that head-start recovery be measured by Akoustis's profits during the head-start period (with avoided costs as a second form), which Qorvo opposed, and Akoustis proposed an instruction barring duplicative damages for the same conduct across claims; Qorvo's UDTPA instruction sought actual loss (replacement-employee and corrective-advertising costs) and unjust enrichment.
object.target: Parties' proposed final jury instructions on unjust enrichment, actual loss and duplicative damages, Qorvo v. Akoustis, D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417 (D.I. 537)

spans.quote: [The measure of recovery is Akoustis’ profits gained during this “head start” period.]
2.11 Trade Secret Damages – Theories of Unjust Enrichment [Disputed] [Akoustis proposes and Qorvo opposes the bracketed language in italics below]
A second form of unjust enrichment is called avoided costs.
[Further, you must not award duplicative damages for the same conduct on multiple claims. You may award damages only if they do not constitute a double recovery for the same conduct.]

In this case, Qorvo claims that its business was affected and that it suffered monetary loss due to the cost to recruit, hire, and train additional employees based on Akoustis’s unlawful hiring of Qorvo employees. Qorvo also seeks recovery of the cost of advertising to correct Akoustis’s false advertisements.

payload.fact: The jury's verdict in Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417): liability findings on each claim and the dollar amounts entered for unjust enrichment, exemplary damages, conspiracy, false advertising and patent damages, and the date and amount of any judgment entered.
payload.why_pivotal: Akoustis had $15.2M of cash at 31 March 2024 against Qorvo claims of about $67.5M in compensatory damages before enhancement. The company says an adverse judgment could force it to curtail operations or file for bankruptcy. A final money judgment over $10.0M left unpaid and unstayed for 60 days is an event of default on the $44.0M notes. The verdict therefore decides whether the June–August 2024 Slope installments are paid from ordinary cash or put at risk.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Completed special verdict form, the minute entry of the verdict, the judgment entered under Rule 58, or an Akoustis 8-K reporting the verdict.
payload.if_resolved: A defense verdict or small award leaves the baseline cash path intact, and the installments are paid from receipts and cash on hand. An award in the tens of millions creates an outflow Akoustis cannot fund from cash. That would start the notes' judgment-default clock (60 days after final judgment, plus notice) unless execution is stayed, and would raise the chance of a bankruptcy filing before the 15 August 2024 final installment.

payload.fact: Whether Akoustis can stay execution of any judgment (bond or other security) and whether it can raise equity after the verdict (ATM sales or an underwritten offering). This includes the amount and timing of any proceeds between 15 May and 15 August 2024.
payload.why_pivotal: Akoustis has no committed funding beyond an ATM with $48.0M notionally remaining, and the sales agents have no obligation to sell. The stock was at about $0.60 in early May 2024 and below Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum. After an adverse verdict, a stay and fresh equity decide whether cash covers operations plus the Slope installments.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Post-verdict 8-Ks, a motion for stay of execution and the court's order on it, ATM sales disclosures, or an underwritten-offering prospectus supplement.
payload.if_resolved: A stay without a large cash bond, plus successful raises, keeps cash above operating needs through August 2024. With no stay and no raise, cash is likely to be used up or a petition filed, stopping further draws and putting unpaid installments into a bankruptcy claim.

payload.fact: Akoustis's damages expert's (Carlyn Irwin's) figure for trade-secret damages, which is redacted in the public filings. It is the defense's quantified alternative to Qorvo's $66.1M.
payload.why_pivotal: The jury's award is likely to fall between the parties' figures. Without the defense number, the lower end of the plausible award range cannot be anchored above zero.
payload.acceptable_evidence: An unredacted expert report or brief, trial testimony transcript, or a company disclosure of the defense damages estimate.
payload.if_resolved: It narrows the award distribution. A defense figure below $10.0M would mean an award at that level does not trip the notes' $10.0M judgment-default threshold.

payload.summary:
Review of Slope's reusable supplier-payment line to Akoustis Technologies, Inc. as of 14 May 2024.
- The dominant external event is Qorvo's D. Del. action (1:21-cv-01417). It was commenced 4 Oct 2021, and the jury trial began 6 May 2024; it was on day 7 on 14 May with no verdict.
- Qorvo claims $66.1M of trade-secret head-start unjust enrichment. It restates the same $66.1M under its civil conspiracy and UDTPA claims. It also claims $279,808 in patent royalty, $1,146,604 in corrective advertising and $809,772 in poaching costs, plus exemplary/punitive damages (DTSA up to 2x), treble patent damages, fees, costs, interest and an injunction.
- On 14 May (D.I. 590) the court barred any compensable UDTPA damages. Earlier, false marking and RICO were dismissed on summary judgment, and the asserted patent claims were held not invalid.
- Both damages experts were admitted. Akoustis says Qorvo is owed nothing on the patents; its own expert's figure is redacted. Its general counsel said an "eight-figure verdict" is possible if the jury adopts Qorvo's experts.
- Akoustis had $15.2M of cash at 31 Mar 2024, has recorded no accrual for the case and discloses substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. It states an adverse judgment could force it to curtail or cease operations and seek bankruptcy protection.
- Funding is uncommitted: $48.0M remains on the ATM, but the agents have no obligation to sell. The stock is below Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum (second compliance deadline 21 Oct 2024), and the January 2024 raise was priced at $0.50 for about $10.4M net.
- The $44.0M 6% convertible notes default if final money judgments over $10.0M (net of insurance) stay unpaid and unstayed for 60 days, after notice by the trustee or holders of 25%. Delisting is also an event of default, and bankruptcy accelerates automatically. Holders can require a cash repurchase at par within 20–35 business days of the notice after a fundamental change. Note interest has been paid in shares ($1.32M in the nine months to March).
- Akoustis's own E.D. Tex. claim against Qorvo is early-stage, with no amount stated.
- The dispute is grouped as dispute_002, with 52 of 54 record items filled. The notes are compiled as financing_001. Validated effects are eff_004 (share-settled interest, no cash) and eff_007 (equity-funding constraint). eff_008 (Texas claim, zero receipt) is escalated for the reviewer.

Whether Akoustis obtains a stay of execution and on what security, and whether it can raise equity (ATM/underwritten offering) after the verdict before the 15 Aug 2024 final installment
Akoustis's damages expert's redacted trade-secret damages figure (lower anchor of the award range)
Whether the court (DTSA) or jury (NCTSPA/conspiracy) adds exemplary or punitive damages, fees and interest
Whether Akoustis regains Nasdaq bid-price compliance by 21 Oct 2024 (notes listing default)
payload.conclusion:
As of 14 May 2024 the jury trial in Qorvo v. Akoustis was under way with no verdict.
- **Qorvo's claims:** $66.1M of trade-secret unjust enrichment (the same figure repeated under conspiracy and UDTPA), $279,808 of patent royalty and $1,146,604 of corrective advertising. It also seeks exemplary damages (up to 2x under the DTSA), treble patent damages, fees, interest and an injunction. By derived arithmetic, the non-duplicative compensatory claims total about $67.5M. On 14 May the court held there is no basis for compensable UDTPA damages.
- **Defense position:** Akoustis contends Qorvo is owed no patent damages. Its general counsel said an eight-figure verdict is possible if the jury adopts Qorvo's experts.
- **Liquidity:** Akoustis had $15.2M of cash at 31 March 2024, recorded no accrual for the case and discloses substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. It states an adverse judgment could lead it to curtail or cease operations and seek bankruptcy protection.
- **Notes:** a final money judgment over $10.0M that stays unpaid and unstayed for 60 days, after notice, is an event of default on its $44.0M convertible notes and permits acceleration.
- **Equity access:** the stock is below the Nasdaq $1.00 minimum, with compliance due by 21 October 2024; the company says failing to regain compliance would materially impair its ability to raise capital. The validated funding-constraint effect therefore does not assume equity inflows.
- **Excluded from cash:** note interest was settled in stock, so no cash outflow is modeled for it. Akoustis's Texas claim against Qorvo has a pending motion to dismiss and no stated amount.
- **Inference flagged:** the roughly two-week trial length is inferred from the juror-lunch order.
- **Open facts:** the verdict amounts, any stay of execution or post-verdict equity raise, and the defense's redacted damages figure.

disputes.reason: disputed effect eff_008 (receipt delay): The effect moves no cash (cash_direction none): it records, for the reviewer, that Akoustis's Texas claim against Qorvo produces no receipt in the loan horizon. The finding's 'alleged' posture is exactly why no receipt is modeled; the guard's requirement of a completed/contractual posture fits effects that move cash, not a documented zero. No mechanism in the list fits a pending claim with no cash effect.
